proposal.reactor_type: Single continuous tubular coil reactor (oil-bath or heated aluminum block), telescoped oxidation/amidation in one heated zone
proposal.tubing_material: PFA (chemically resistant to H2SO4, TBHP, dioxane)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Based on total combined liquid flow rate (1.0 mL/min) after mixing all reagent streams; reaction is fully liquid-phase, no gas co-feed
proposal.light_setup: None (thermally driven reaction, no photochemical step)

streams.contents: Benzyl alcohol (0.889 M), morpholine (0.889 M), NaBr (0.13 M, 0.15 equiv), H2SO4 (0.18 M, 0.2 equiv)
TBHP (70 wt% aqueous, ~8.0 M as delivered)

proposal.mixer_type: Low-dead-volume PEEK or stainless T-mixer (or Y-mixer), immediately upstream of heated coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Alcohol and amine are pre-mixed with the NaBr/H2SO4 catalyst package (Stream 1) because they do not react without an oxidant; TBHP is held in a separate stream (Stream 2) and combined only just before the heated reactor to prevent premature exothermic decomposition or oxidation during storage/handling and to allow precise stoichiometric control of oxidant equivalents at the point of reaction.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas dioxane feed to minimize dissolved O2 interference with radical bromate/TBHP chemistry
Pre-filter NaBr solution to remove undissolved solids that could clog microchannels
Preheat Stream 1 to 50 °C before mixing to prevent localized precipitation of morpholine sulfate salts on contact with H2SO4
post_reactor_steps: In-line cooling (heat exchanger) to <30 °C before pressure letdown
Quench with aqueous Na2S2O3 (or NaHSO3) to destroy residual TBHP before BPR to avoid gas evolution downstream
Liquid-liquid phase separation (aqueous NaBr/H2SO4/Na2SO4 vs. organic dioxane/product)
Optional in-line FTIR or UV/Vis monitoring for real-time conversion tracking
Standard workup: solvent evaporation, aqueous wash, and recrystallization/chromatography to isolate benzoylmorpholine
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a telescoped one-pot oxidative amidation: (1) NaBr/H2SO4 generates a transient hypobromite/bromate species from TBHP that oxidizes benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde; (2) benzaldehyde condenses with morpholine to form a hemiaminal, which is further oxidized in situ by excess TBHP to the corresponding amide (benzoylmorpholine). The acidic bromide system serves a dual catalytic role in both steps, consistent with the original batch mechanism.

stage_parameters.stage: Alcohol oxidation (in situ, first ~5 min of coil)
Oxidative amidation (remaining ~25 min of same coil)

reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_and_volume: Total flow (1.0 mL/min) and reactor volume (30 mL) were chosen to reproduce the batch 30-min residence time at 80 °C on a lab-scale continuous system with manageable coil length (~9.5 m at 2.0 mm ID).
reasoning_per_field.stream_split: TBHP is dosed as a separate stream for safety (controlled addition, avoids premixed peroxide/acid instability) while alcohol, amine, and catalysts are combined upstream since they are unreactive without oxidant.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_assumptions: Batch reported an overall 0.667 M substrate concentration with unspecified TBHP/NaBr/H2SO4 loadings; standard literature loadings (3 equiv TBHP, 0.15 equiv NaBr, 0.2 equiv H2SO4) were assumed and back-calculated to preserve the final 0.667 M target after stream mixing.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_setting: 8 bar chosen to suppress dioxane boiling (bp 101 °C) and vapor-phase O2/TBHP decomposition products at 80 °C, ensuring stable single-phase liquid flow.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID: 2.0 mm selected to balance reasonable coil length, adequate heat transfer, and resistance to clogging from any transient salt precipitation.

proposal.literature_analogies: Design inspired by continuous-flow TBHP-mediated oxidative amidation and Kabachnik-type telescoped oxidation/condensation platforms (e.g., Kappe-group flow oxidations using TBHP/NaBr systems and telescoped alcohol-to-amide continuous syntheses reported in Org. Process Res. Dev.), where alcohol oxidation and amine coupling are combined in a single heated residence coil with staged reagent introduction for safety.
safety_flags: TBHP is a strong oxidizer capable of exothermic decomposition at 80 °C, releasing O2 and heat — pressure relief and temperature interlocks required.
NaBr/H2SO4 combination may generate trace Br2/HBr vapors — reactor effluent should be vented through a scrubber or handled in a fume hood.
H2SO4 is corrosive; ensure all wetted components (pumps, fittings) are PFA/PTFE or acid-resistant.
Maintain BPR integrity to prevent flash boiling or gas pocket formation from TBHP decomposition products.
Include a rupture disk or pressure relief valve on the reactor outlet as a fail-safe.
